title: Svalbard: the fastest-warming place
bn: স্বালবার্ড: সবচেয়ে দ্রুত উষ্ণ হওয়া জায়গা
note: Arctic air warms several times faster than the world average. Check the weather-station witness too.

title: Arctic sea ice every September
note: September is when Arctic ice is smallest. Watch the record lows pile up after 2005.

title: North India: warming hills, cooling plains
bn: উত্তর ভারত: পাহাড় উষ্ণ, সমভূমি শীতল
note: The box average hides opposite trends: look at the coloured grid cells. Haze and irrigation on the plains can cool the air.

title: East Africa: wetter here, drier there
bn: পূর্ব আফ্রিকা: কোথাও ভেজা, কোথাও শুকনো
note: One region, rain trends in both directions. The grid cells show where.

title: Kolkata rain: two witnesses disagree
note: NASA's model says much wetter; the Dum Dum rain gauge does not. A real detective checks a second witness.

title: Pearl River mouth: a greener sea
bn: পার্ল নদীর মোহনা: সবুজ হচ্ছে সাগর
note: NASA scientists found this river's coastal chlorophyll rising while most others fell (Acker et al. 2009). Is it still true?

title: Mississippi mouth: the dead-zone river
note: Farm fertiliser feeds plankton blooms here, which leave a low-oxygen dead zone each summer.

title: Ganges–Brahmaputra mouth: the sea off Bangladesh
note: The world's biggest river delta. Mud from the rivers colours the water as much as plankton does.

title: Dhaka: fewer scorching days, more sticky ones
bn: ঢাকা: প্রচণ্ড গরম দিন কম, ভ্যাপসা গরম দিন বেশি
note: Humid-heat days rose while 35 °C days fell: switch the variable to 'Hot days' to see the opposite trend in the same place.

title: Tangail: losing green
note: MODIS sees this district getting less green. Compare with Shariatpur, about 120 km away, which is getting greener.

title: Shariatpur: getting greener
note: The opposite of Tangail, in the same country and the same years.

title: Brahmanbaria: hotter ground
note: MODIS daytime ground temperature at the district centre, measured from space every 8 days.
